status: one-seed 31-output-token extended-optimization diagnostic; not a headline result

gate_audit.task_learnability: pass: direct text reaches 1.0 exact match and 1.0 satisfaction in every quartile
gate_audit.causal_z_use: provisional pass at one seed: correct Z improves satisfaction by .086 over shuffled Z
gate_audit.z_task_optimization: fail: Z exact match remains zero and satisfaction rises only .005 relative to the 40-epoch pilot
gate_audit.persistence: fail to establish: correct Z declines .058 and remains far below the perfect direct control
gate_audit.decision: do not launch longer horizons; test whether structured or query-dependent latent access repairs the 31-token deficit

interpretation: Extended optimization completely removes the direct control's apparent position-dependent drift, proving that the scheduled task is learnable.
The same extension barely changes single-vector late-layer Z, which remains unable to produce any complete 31-token sequence.
The .086 shuffled-Z effect shows that the generator uses Z, but causal use is not sufficient for accurate scheduled retrieval.

A plausible mechanism is that one globally added vector is poorly suited to selecting different facet values in response to a varying query sequence; this requires direct comparison with structured latent access before any longer-horizon sweep.
